title: Bug: [SmartSwitch] Huge memory increase in systemd-networkd
author: vivekkarri
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

On SmartSwitch Platform, we observe systemd-networkd memory to increase after running the tests.  This is rarely seen. Only seen twice until now in our regression. 

It was seen once on `stress/test_stress_routes.py` and once on `generic_config_updater/test_bgp_prefix.py:: test_bgp_prefix_tc1_suite`

### Steps to Reproduce

- Run either of these tests. Check the total memory used before and after the test. 
- With very low probability, you might see a huge increase in systemd-networkd memory and total memory

```
Pre-test: 
    PID USER      PR  NI    VIRT    RES    SHR S  %CPU  %MEM     TIME+ COMMAND
   2229 systemd+  20   0  842720 778628  10412 S   0.0   0.6  22:11.54 systemd+

Post-test:
    PID USER      PR  NI    VIRT    RES    SHR S  %CPU  %MEM     TIME+ COMMAND
   2229 systemd+  20   0 2444616   2.3g  10444 D  28.6   1.8  22:54.84 systemd+
```

```
Failed: [ALARM]: free:used memory usage increased by 2040.0%, exceeds increase threshold 20%% (previous: 6862.0 MB, current: 8902.0 MB)
```


### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Test fails saying

```
Failed: [ALARM]: free:used memory usage increased by 2040.0%, exceeds increase threshold 20%% (previous: 6862.0 MB, current: 8902.0 MB)
```

### Triage

Both the instances seem to happen during BGP tests and route churn. 

Empirical evidence shows the correlation between FRR and systemd-networkd

https://scottstuff.net/posts/2025/02/25/frr-vs-systemd-networkd/
We also has a similar issue where huge number of logs are seen from systemd-networkd seen (https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/23130). However, that seems to be fixing it. 

If this were to happen seen, test with ManageForeignNetxtHops=No set to systemd-networkd. 

However,  we can't yet completely prove that this can fix the problem

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it

Disable Foreign Nexthops in systemd-networkd

```
ManageForeignNextHops=
      A boolean. When true, systemd-networkd will remove nexthops that are not configured in .network files (except for routes with protocol "kernel"). When false, it will not remove any foreign nexthops, keeping them even if they are not configured in a .network file. Defaults to yes.
      Added in version 256.
```
